name: gaussian_majorana_global_resynthesis
precondition: family dv_angle; needs rotations; measurement_free; 2 <= qubits <= 8; and the op list must be fermionic-Gaussian as a whole, i.e. v4.api.fermion.is_gaussian(ops) is true: every Clifford in it maps Majorana monomials g_a -> +-g_b (h, s, sdg, z, x, cx/cz in the JW-local pattern) and every rotation's front-frame Pauli (v4.api.pauli.frames) is a Majorana BILINEAR, bilinear_of(P, n) != None. Circuits with any rotation whose Pauli is a weight-4-or-higher non-bilinear monomial are excluded and cost nothing. On tfim_6 the fingerprint already reports free_fermion = true, majorana_planes = 12, generator_algebra_rank = 22.
identity: A Gaussian circuit on n qubits is, in the 2n Majorana operators g_1..g_2n, a single element R of O(2n): U g_a U^dag = sum_b R_{ba} g_b. Compose the whole op list ONCE into that R (orthogonal_of(ops)), then re-emit U from R instead of from its 160 gates: Givens-factor R into at most 2n(2n-1)/2 = 66 adjacent-plane rotations G(a, a+1, theta_i) times a residual sign diagonal (givens(R)), and emit each plane rotation as the one-parameter Gaussian gate exp(theta_i g_a g_{a+1} / 2) = plane_rotation(a, a+1, theta_i, n) -- a single Rz conjugated by a fixed Clifford (JW string), one non-Clifford rotation each. The residual sign diagonal is a product of Z/S gates: pure Clifford, free. Plane rotations whose theta is a multiple of pi/4 (on_grid) are emitted as Clifford/T and cost nothing extra. Drop them from the Rz tally. The output op list replaces the entire circuit (the rule is one global match, not a window): trigger returns the single match {whole circuit} when the precondition holds and the emitted rotation count is strictly below the current one.
correctness: Gaussian (matchgate / free-fermion) unitaries form a group: a product of exponentials of Majorana bilinears is the exponential of a bilinear, and the adjoint action on the 2n-dimensional real Majorana span is a faithful homomorphism onto SO(2n) (O(2n) once the parity/sign diagonal is included), with kernel exactly the global phase. Therefore R determines U up to global phase, which is unobservable (invariant 6) and which the judge's phase-aligned distance already quotients out. Givens' theorem factors any R in O(2n) exactly into adjacent plane rotations times a sign diagonal; each plane rotation lifts back to exp(theta g_a g_{a+1} / 2) by the same homomorphism. So the re-emitted op list equals the original up to phase: the identity is exact, not a fit, and the angles are read off R by arctan2, not optimised. The only error is float round-off in forming R (~1e-14, orders below any ledger charge); the judge's phase-aligned operator distance on the whole-circuit check confirms it, and the rule declines (returns no match) if that distance exceeds 1e-12 rather than drawing from the budget. Ancilla-free, measurement-free, so the specification contract is the unitary one.
trigger: One match per circuit. Fires when: (1) every op is in {h, s, sdg, x, z, cx, cz, rz, t, tdg} with no measurement; (2) frames(ops) gives, for every rotation record, a Pauli P with bilinear_of(P, n) != None; (3) orthogonal_of(ops) returns an R with R^T R = I to 1e-10; (4) len(givens(R) rotations with not on_grid(theta)) < number of current non-Clifford rotations. On tfim_6: 160 off-grid Rz in, at most 66 (expected 22-66, since generator_algebra_rank = 22 bounds the plane-rotation support actually used) out.
expected_effect: The 160 off-grid Rz collapse to the at most 66 Givens plane rotations of the single O(12) element (22 if the rank-22 generator algebra means R lives in a 22-dimensional subgroup, which the fingerprint's generator_algebra_rank = 22 against 66 for full O(12) suggests). The 180 cx / 192 h / 102 sdg / 29 s / 12 z Clifford skeleton is replaced by the JW conjugation strings of the emitted plane rotations plus one sign diagonal, which also cuts CNOT count (tie-break 3). The T saving is double: fewer rotations to synthesize, AND each surviving rotation gets a larger eps_rz = (eps/2)/N_Rz because N_Rz fell, so gridsynth pays ~3*log2(160/N_Rz) fewer T on each one. At N_Rz = 66: 66 * ~50 T = ~3300 T total, versus 8560 now. At N_Rz = 22: ~1370 T.
source: Terhal & DiVincenzo, 'Classical simulation of noninteracting-fermion quantum circuits', PRA 65 032325 (2002); Jozsa & Miyake, 'Matchgates and classical simulation of quantum circuits', Proc. R. Soc. A 464 (2008); Givens/Thouless decomposition of O(2n) as in Kivlichan et al., 'Quantum simulation of electronic structure with linear depth and connectivity', PRL 120 110501 (2018)
notes: This is lever (c) on the one circuit where levers (a) and (b) have exactly zero headroom: pyzx/TKET/BQSKit all sit at 8560 and DPF is worse (9600) because snapping 160 individually-cheap angles buys nothing. None of them represent the circuit as a group element, so none can see that 160 rotations parameterise an object with at most 66 parameters. The floor's Pauli-frame merging is local axis matching and cannot do this: the merged axes here are 22 distinct bilinear classes with 160 parity classes, all already fully folded (foldable_remaining = 0).
